analysis.title: Strategic: Strengthen your core
key_insights: UBS CIO argues a diversified core portfolio lets investors handle several market scenarios in 2027 without depending on one path for growth and rates.

Base case: economic growth and corporate earnings stay resilient, AI investment keeps rising, and inflation moderates. UBS sees a constructive return outlook for stocks and bonds, with enough dispersion within and between markets to require diversification.

Favorable scenarios named: stronger AI productivity, lower inflation and easier monetary policy, supporting equities, credit, industrial commodities and infrastructure. Adverse scenario named: persistent inflation forcing rates higher, pressuring equities and government bonds while favoring select energy, materials and infrastructure assets.

The largest companies are around 40% of the S&P 500, so a portfolio concentrated in US megacap technology is also concentrated in AI investment and earnings expectations being met. UBS recommends broader exposure across regions, sectors and styles.
UBS sees industrials benefiting from spending on automation, defense, electrification and infrastructure, and health care as having an earnings profile less dependent on the investment cycle.

Yields have reset higher, including a renewed rise in 2026, which improves the role of bonds. Higher starting yields raise income, give a cushion if rates rise further, and leave room for price gains if inflation moderates, growth weakens or central banks cut.

UBS rates high grade (HG) and investment grade (IG) bonds Attractive, favoring short- and medium-duration high-quality bonds and staying more cautious on the longest maturities because of fiscal concerns and elevated issuance.

UBS also rates high yield (HY) and emerging market bonds Attractive, citing elevated yields and resilient aggregate fundamentals. It notes HY behaves more like stocks and EM debt adds sovereign, credit and liquidity risk.
Bonds diversify equity losses best when inflation is low or stable. If inflation stays elevated and rates rise, stocks and bonds can fall together.

For markets with low local sovereign yields, such as Switzerland, UBS suggests income strategies across equities, fixed income and derivatives, and says gold or structured strategies with capital preservation features may be prudent.

Completion assets (hedge funds, commodities, gold, infrastructure, real estate) should each do a defined job. UBS cautions that hedge fund diversification depends on strategy and manager selection, cyclical commodities can fall when growth slows, higher rates can weigh on infrastructure and real estate valuations, and private investments carry illiquidity and leverage risks.

A 60/40 US equity-bond portfolio invested in 2020 would have drifted to roughly 80/20 if left untouched. UBS recommends regular rebalancing to restore the intended risk profile and limit concentration.

sector_views.rationale: May benefit from spending on automation, defense, electrification and infrastructure.
Earnings profile is less dependent on the investment cycle, which UBS presents as a diversifier.

earnings_insights: Base case assumes corporate earnings remain resilient in 2027. No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.reading: Moderating path (base case, no figure given)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a constructive return outlook for stocks and bonds. Persistent inflation is the adverse scenario, which would push rates higher and hurt equities and government bonds.
Underpins earnings resilience and AI investment in the base case.

risk_factors: Persistent inflation forcing rates higher, which can push stocks and bonds down together.
Concentration in US megacap technology and dependence on AI investment and earnings expectations being met.
Fiscal concerns and elevated issuance weighing on the longest-maturity bonds.
Higher interest rates weighing on infrastructure and real estate valuations and raising refinancing costs.
Illiquidity, limited disclosure, uncertain cash flows, leverage, capital calls and blind-pool risk in private investments.
Cyclical commodities can suffer when growth slows.
vol_and_positioning: Concentration: the largest companies are around 40% of the S&P 500, which makes US megacap-heavy portfolios dependent on AI investment and earnings expectations.
geopolitical: Geopolitics is listed among the factors, with inflation, central bank policy and government debt, that will drive market moves in 2027. No specific event or region is named.

key_data_points.metric: Share of the S&P 500 represented by the largest companies
key_data_points.context: Used to argue that portfolios concentrated in US megacap technology depend heavily on AI investment and earnings expectations.
key_data_points.anchor: With the largest companies representing around 40% of the S&P 500

key_data_points.metric: Drifted equity/bond mix of a 60/40 US portfolio left untouched since 2020
key_data_points.context: Illustrates the need for regular rebalancing after equities outperformed.
key_data_points.anchor: A 60/40 US equity-bond portfolio invested in 2020 would have drifted to approximately 80/20 if left

tension_points.bull_case: If growth weakens and inflation moderates, high-quality bond prices may rise as equities come under pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: If inflation remains elevated and interest rates rise, stocks and bonds can decline together.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation staying elevated with rates rising would break the bond hedge.

theme_stances.key_argument: A diversified, regularly rebalanced core with selective completion assets avoids requiring one company, asset class or forecast to be right.
Higher starting yields raise income and add a cushion, favoring short- and medium-duration high-quality bonds over the longest maturities.
theme_stances.evidence: We currently view HG and IG bonds as Attractive.

contextual_mentions: renewed rise in bond yields in 2026
gold and structured strategies as diversifiers
data center exposure via infrastructure and real estate
Swiss low-yield income generation using derivatives
fiscal concerns and elevated issuance on long-duration bonds
